scope: Whole-spine editorial contribution map. Roles and proposed uses are authored; floor order, room artifacts and teaching-plan context are read live. This grants no new game tools.

rows.title: An origin, already running
rows.learn: A location and a count give the encounter a reference.
rows.carry: A place to begin; no construction stock yet.
rows.test: Can we distinguish the point from the machine counting frames?

capabilities.title: Origin and frame count
capabilities.detail: Existing rooftop counter and YOU ARE HERE encounter.

rows.title: One point, six possibilities
rows.learn: A joint offers six axis-aligned directions.
rows.carry: The first joint, a saved construction and BUILD from hand scale to full size.
rows.test: Place a neighbour, undo it, and find the same construction at the next bench.

capabilities.title: Six-port point
capabilities.detail: Reusable stock in the Points edition. Neighbours lie one or two metres away.

capabilities.title: Carry a saved construction
capabilities.detail: The blueprint is shared between bench editions. Full-size output is rebuilt with BUILD after unloading.

capabilities.title: Full-size BUILD
capabilities.detail: BUILD creates a full-size copy from the same 1:10 hand model. Floor 20 later adds the glass bay; output is never scaled to fit.

rows.title: A point has an address
rows.learn: Position belongs to a reference frame.
rows.carry: A way to describe where each joint is.
rows.test: Move the black point and read what changes in x, y and z.

capabilities.title: Coordinate address
capabilities.detail: Basin, held black point and coordinate readout exist; a workbench coordinate inspector is still to be connected.

rows.title: Two lengths, one grid
rows.learn: Two addressed endpoints determine a connection.
rows.carry: Separate 1 m and 2 m rods.
rows.test: Make a two-metre side once with a long rod, then with two short rods.

capabilities.title: 1 m rod
capabilities.detail: 10 cm in the 1:10 hand model; one metre in the world.

capabilities.title: 2 m rod
capabilities.detail: 20 cm in the hand model; two metres in the world.

capabilities.title: Square frame
capabilities.detail: Four corners and closed sides. A side can be one long rod or two short rods; occupied segments cannot overlap.

rows.title: Trace: an antithesis to the frame
rows.learn: The fixed frame and the free trace offer different ways to occupy space. A gesture can leave a mark without becoming a beam.
rows.carry: A counterpoint to the measured structure: drawn traces, replay and an expressive presence beside the grid.
rows.test: Draw across and away from the grid. Replay the gesture without forcing it onto the rod lattice.

capabilities.title: Drawn trace and replay
capabilities.detail: Drawing and replay exist. We read the trace as an antithesis to the fixed scaffold: a continuous gesture with its own history, not compulsory construction stock. This role is an interpretation of the encounter.

rows.title: Half a square becomes a surface
rows.learn: Three vertices define a face; two complementary halves close a square.
rows.carry: A right-triangle panel in XY, XZ or YZ.
rows.test: Fill one half, then its complement; an unclosed frame must reject the panel.

capabilities.title: Triangular half-face
capabilities.detail: Fixed diagonal, 1 × 1 m or 2 × 2 m square frame. This is different from the equilateral folded-edge table.

capabilities.title: Folded-edge assembly
capabilities.detail: The retained TriangleTable explores folding; it is not yet a folding tool for the saved workshop graph.

rows.title: A solid can block or help
rows.learn: The same family of solids produces different bodily relations: a pyramid interrupts a route; a wedge makes a rise walkable.
rows.carry: Pyramid as obstacle, wedge as stepping aid, and a tetrahedral corner as a separate proposed joint.
rows.test: Walk around the pyramid, then use the wedge’s 2 m run to reach a 1 m rise. Do not mistake either prefab for an unlocked bench part.

capabilities.title: Pyramid blocker
capabilities.detail: The obstruction area places PyramidBlocker. Its role is to redirect a body around a solid, rather than fill every scaffold bay.

capabilities.title: Tetrahedral corner
capabilities.detail: Needs diagonal or angled joints and non-axis-aligned faces. The six-port workshop cannot currently make it.

capabilities.title: Walkable wedge / slope
capabilities.detail: The support area already stages a 2 m run / 1 m rise. Reuse this slope to reach a box or platform; a shared workbench wedge attachment is still to be connected.

rows.title: Close the frame faster
rows.learn: A whole quad replaces two halves of the same face.
rows.carry: Full quads; a closed cube assembled from existing parts.
rows.test: Build six faces and check the corners and collision. An enclosure is not a filled volume.

capabilities.title: Full square quad
capabilities.detail: One empty 1 × 1 m or 2 × 2 m framed face; cannot overlap a half already there.

capabilities.title: Six-face cube
capabilities.detail: Buildable from points, rods and quads. It is an enclosure, not a new stock type.

capabilities.title: Filled cube block
capabilities.detail: A separate solid-volume or reusable grouped-cube tool is not in the current workshop vocabulary.

rows.title: Forms that need not hold anything up
rows.learn: A primitive can be an ornament, a strange attachment or a companion form. Its value need not be structural.
rows.carry: A vocabulary of potential decorations, kept separate from the five structural stock types.
rows.test: Place a decorative form beside a familiar frame: does it change the place without silently claiming to support it?

capabilities.title: Primitive forms / possible decorations
capabilities.detail: The hall has spheres, cylinders and other primitive forms. Reading them as decorations is a proposed use; existing forms are not automatically compatible workshop attachments.

capabilities.title: Attach a primitive decoration
capabilities.detail: Reuse an existing primitive as an optional attachment. Give it an attachment location and explicit collision behaviour without making it a required support.

rows.title: A support can vary
rows.learn: A repeated support can keep its role while changing its form.
rows.carry: A column as an architectural member.
rows.test: Replace a support and inspect both the joint and the clearance.

capabilities.title: Column / repeated support
capabilities.detail: Existing column encounter. A selectable workshop column recipe is not yet integrated.

rows.title: A section travels
rows.learn: A cross-section and a path generate a member.
rows.carry: A way to distinguish a rail from a solid block.
rows.test: Compare two profiles along the same path.

capabilities.title: Extruded profile
capabilities.detail: Profile artifacts exist; applying a chosen section to saved rods remains a proposed extension.

rows.title: An opening is constructed too
rows.learn: A boundary can frame a passage.
rows.carry: Clearance, an inside and an outside.
rows.test: Walk through the opening and check that visible and physical boundaries agree.

capabilities.title: Opening / passage
capabilities.detail: Existing portal encounter and span; automatic cutting of workshop panels is not implemented.

rows.title: Compose with what remains
rows.learn: A finite set of forms allows many arrangements.
rows.carry: A personal construction assembled from the accumulated kit.
rows.test: Reopen the saved work and explain which parts are stock, assemblies or props.

rows.title: A cube you can take with you
rows.learn: A body can be picked up and displaced. It can also become a container for a concealed possibility.
rows.carry: The existing pickup cube; a proposed secret-bearing version that releases a power-up when deliberately activated.
rows.test: First pick up and replace the ordinary cube. For the proposed container, reveal its content once and preserve that state after reload.

capabilities.title: Pickup cube
capabilities.detail: The hall includes pick_up_cube. Carrying an object is a useful action in its own right, not just a demonstration of moving the scaffold.

capabilities.title: Cube with a hidden power-up
capabilities.detail: A Mario-like use for the pickup cube: an intentional action reveals a concealed reward. The activation rule, reward and persistent opened state still need implementation.

rows.title: Three operations, different effects
rows.learn: Translation, rotation and scale act on a body in different ways.
rows.carry: A distinction between pose and size.
rows.test: Change one operation at a time and compare the result.

capabilities.title: Transform operations
capabilities.detail: Existing introductory structures; workshop transforms remain separate from the authored course motors.

rows.title: A bridge carries its passenger
rows.learn: Change position while retaining the rigid assembly.
rows.carry: A moving deck and its path.
rows.test: Board, ride and step off; the body and passenger must stay related.

capabilities.title: Translation / moving bridge
capabilities.detail: Native playground translation is implemented and tested. Attaching a translation motor to any saved build is proposed.

rows.title: Choose what turns around what
rows.learn: The pivot and parent-child relation determine the motion.
rows.carry: A rotating bridge and a hinge.
rows.test: Move the pivot and observe how the same deck sweeps a different space.

capabilities.title: Pivot rotation and parented folding
capabilities.detail: Authored rotating and folding assemblies exist. A player-assigned hinge on saved work is not implemented.

rows.title: Size changes the encounter
rows.learn: Scale changes dimensions and bodily clearance.
rows.carry: An understanding of size, distinct from adding a longer rod.
rows.test: Compare scaling a body with replacing a 1 m rod by a 2 m rod.

capabilities.title: Scale / body clearance
capabilities.detail: Existing scale chambers and carousels. The authorized scaffold keeps rods at their actual stock lengths.

rows.title: The body is a measuring instrument
rows.learn: An opening is different for a different body.
rows.carry: A clearance test for what we build.
rows.test: Can this body pass through the aperture it made?

capabilities.title: Body-relative clearance
capabilities.detail: Existing approach, aperture and carving examples; the workbench does not yet offer a body-clearance probe.

rows.title: Movement meets an obstruction
rows.learn: A moving boundary can carry, block or push another body.
rows.carry: Collision as a consequence of the chosen motion.
rows.test: Change a moving obstacle and predict where contact will occur.

capabilities.title: Moving boundaries and contact
capabilities.detail: Existing pushers, launchers and crossing mechanisms. They are examples, not stock in the workshop tray.

rows.title: Build small. Walk the consequence.
rows.learn: The hand model and the full-size result use the same construction.
rows.carry: Glass test bay, physical support test and an authored moving playground.
rows.test: BUILD the model, DROP TEST the result, revise the unsupported case.

capabilities.title: DROP TEST
capabilities.detail: A real falling ball tests contact and support. It does not calculate bending or structural stress.

capabilities.title: Attach a motor to my build
capabilities.detail: The missing handoff between a saved construction and the moving bridges already in the course.

rows.title: Something happens; something responds
rows.learn: An event can trigger a consequence.
rows.carry: A proposed trigger attached to our structure.
rows.test: Cross a threshold and see one explicit response.

capabilities.title: Event / trigger
capabilities.detail: The event encounter is staged. A reusable event component in the building kit is still to be connected.

rows.title: Both conditions must hold
rows.learn: Two inputs constrain one consequence.
rows.carry: A proposed two-condition gate for a bridge.
rows.test: Try neither, either one, and both inputs.

capabilities.title: AND / two conditions
capabilities.detail: Existing matter-spring AND apparatus; not a workshop wiring socket yet.

rows.title: Another way, or an interruption
rows.learn: OR admits an alternative; NOT changes the condition.
rows.carry: Alternative routes and interruptible mechanisms.
rows.test: Demonstrate the cases where one route is enough and where a signal prevents action.

capabilities.title: OR / either condition
capabilities.detail: Existing OR apparatus.

capabilities.title: NOT / inverted condition
capabilities.detail: Existing NOT apparatus. Wiring these to a carried build remains proposed.

rows.title: Keep the relation between parts
rows.learn: A useful mechanism combines parts and conditions.
rows.carry: A proposed reusable group with its own behaviour.
rows.test: Save and reload the group without losing its internal connections.

capabilities.title: Save a group with behaviour
capabilities.detail: The static workshop blueprint already saves; storing attached conditions and motors requires a shared extension.

rows.title: An address becomes a brush target
rows.learn: An array gives each cell an address. That address can name a mark on an existing surface, as well as an occupied place.
rows.carry: 2D addresses and the proposed grid brush: mark or erase individual cells in black and white before Colour.
rows.test: Select one cell, change only that cell, then find it again by its address. Saving the brush marks on a built panel is a future integration test.

capabilities.title: Indexed slots
capabilities.detail: Existing row, 2D grid and 3D array. Indexed selection of workshop groups is proposed.

capabilities.title: 2D grid brush
capabilities.detail: Use [x,z] to mark or erase a cell on an existing surface. The array encounter supplies addresses and occupancy; an editable brush carried onto workshop panels is not connected yet.

rows.title: Paint occupancy in space
rows.learn: A third address gives a volume of cells. Spatial painting changes where something exists, rather than merely colouring it.
rows.carry: A proposed 3D occupancy brush: add and erase neutral cells while keeping their addresses.
rows.test: Choose a layer and one [x,y,z] cell. Add or erase there without changing its neighbours; preserve empty addresses and the passage through the volume.

capabilities.title: Three-dimensional addressing
capabilities.detail: Existing array flight and open structures. Repetition of a saved workshop group is not yet connected.

capabilities.title: 3D occupancy brush
capabilities.detail: The existing flight lab selects x, y and z and observes removed cells. Turning this into a reversible, saved add/erase brush is proposed; coloured voxels belong to the later palette.

rows.title: The first pattern on a surface
rows.learn: Repeat, turn or invert a motif on a surface that already exists. Pattern is a layer, not another structural part.
rows.carry: The first monochrome surface pattern; apply it to a built face as the next handoff.
rows.test: Change the pattern while keeping the supporting panel, its dimensions and collision unchanged.

capabilities.title: Monochrome motif and repetition
capabilities.detail: Existing tiling-principles artifact; a repeat tool for the saved construction remains proposed.

capabilities.title: Pattern the carried surface
capabilities.detail: Transfer the existing tiling rules onto an identified workshop face. Store the rule and orientation separately from the face geometry.

rows.title: Turn the patterned surface upright
rows.learn: Change the plane while retaining the arrangement rule.
rows.carry: The same motif on a different plane, with its local coordinates and orientation intact.
rows.test: Move the pattern from floor to wall. Check which way its local axes run; keep the opening and the supporting geometry unchanged.

capabilities.title: Repeat on another plane
capabilities.detail: Existing wall examples. The same workshop group should eventually repeat on floor or wall.

rows.title: Build a place around the disco
rows.learn: The disco is the centre of an inhabited place. The scaffold can frame it with edges, platforms and a way in, while the floor keeps its own pattern and clock.
rows.carry: An existing disco installation to build around, rather than another piece to insert into the structural kit.
rows.test: Keep a clear entrance and room to move. Change PLAY / HOLD, ONE STEP and the pattern without rebuilding the surrounding structure.

capabilities.title: Disco / patterned floor with a clock
capabilities.detail: The existing disco controls drive patterns and timing on the floor; before Colour its palette is monochrome. The installation retains its own identity.

capabilities.title: Scaffold around the disco
capabilities.detail: Compose a surround, platforms and approach around the existing installation. Keep the dancing surface and controls accessible; the carried-build placement still needs a trial.

rows.title: Colour the same world three ways
rows.learn: Choose a colour, paint one square, or let a gradient span the structure. These are different scopes for changing appearance; none needs to replace the construction.
rows.carry: A palette, addressed face painting and a gradient field as proposed tools on the same saved structure.
rows.test: Paint one quad, then apply a gradient across several parts. Explicitly choose whether it replaces or preserves local paint; BUILD and reload must retain the choices without changing connections.

capabilities.title: Colour by part or rule
capabilities.detail: The current colour station selects a part and paints it, or colours the existing stack by shape, height or neighbour. These are existing examples, not yet paint tools for the saved scaffold.

capabilities.title: Choose a construction colour
capabilities.detail: Proposed shared palette for rods, joints, panels and ornaments. Preserve member identity and save the assignment alongside geometry.

capabilities.title: Paint an individual square
capabilities.detail: Select a single quad or a grid cell on its surface and assign a chosen colour. Keep face colour and sub-cell marks distinct; record which one the brush addresses.

capabilities.title: Gradient across the structure
capabilities.detail: Use a chosen axis and two endpoints to colour many members as one field. Define its precedence against hand-painted faces; save the rule rather than altering geometry.

rows.title: Light the surface, keep the paint
rows.learn: Illumination and material colour have different owners.
rows.carry: Aim a lamp at a built panel; retain its chosen paint while changing the light.
rows.test: Move one lamp, then restore it. The panel's saved colour must stay fixed.

capabilities.title: Light the surface, keep the paint
capabilities.detail: Aim a lamp at a built panel; retain its chosen paint while changing the light.

rows.title: Choose a colour with a point
rows.learn: A position can be read as three colour channels.
rows.carry: A reachable colour selector that returns a value to any chosen construction member.
rows.test: Pick a known RGB value twice; moving the selector must not repaint unselected members.

capabilities.title: Choose a colour with a point
capabilities.detail: A reachable colour selector that returns a value to any chosen construction member.

rows.title: A palette has an order
rows.learn: An ordered list of colours can divide one fixed extent.
rows.carry: Choose a palette for repeated faces or an ornamental arch, keeping physical size separate.
rows.test: Change from two to four colours while preserving the opening and outside dimensions.

capabilities.title: A palette has an order
capabilities.detail: Choose a palette for repeated faces or an ornamental arch, keeping physical size separate.

rows.title: Sample a colour field
rows.learn: Hand position, field coordinates and colour are three distinct mappings.
rows.carry: Sample a gradient or HSV field before applying its value to a member.
rows.test: Move only one coordinate; predict the channel that changes and test an out-of-range input.

capabilities.title: Sample a colour field
capabilities.detail: Sample a gradient or HSV field before applying its value to a member.

rows.title: Paint one addressed square
rows.learn: Selection can move while earlier cells retain their paint.
rows.carry: Bind the existing palette and per-cell colour record to a scaffold face with stable addresses.
rows.test: Paint two cells, change selection, then reload: each cell must retain its own value.

capabilities.title: Paint one addressed square
capabilities.detail: Bind the existing palette and per-cell colour record to a scaffold face with stable addresses.

rows.title: Paint by contact and aim
rows.learn: A held brush needs both an active action and an accepted surface hit.
rows.carry: A brush for marks on an existing panel, using local surface coordinates.
rows.test: Miss the panel, release the action and drop the brush; each must stop new marks.

capabilities.title: Paint by contact and aim
capabilities.detail: A brush for marks on an existing panel, using local surface coordinates.

rows.title: Compose transparent colour
rows.learn: Appearance depends on paint, overlap and viewpoint as well as placement.
rows.carry: Layer translucent panes and gradients while retaining explicit collision and support.
rows.test: Change alpha, then walk the boundary: transparency must not silently remove collision.

capabilities.title: Compose transparent colour
capabilities.detail: Layer translucent panes and gradients while retaining explicit collision and support.

rows.title: The disco receives its palette
rows.learn: A pattern's values and clock can continue while its palette changes.
rows.carry: Colour the existing disco surrounded by our scaffold; keep palette and phase independent.
rows.test: Make both colours equal, advance phase, then restore contrast and reveal the retained pattern.

capabilities.title: The disco receives its palette
capabilities.detail: Colour the existing disco surrounded by our scaffold; keep palette and phase independent.

rows.title: One source, many surfaces
rows.learn: Editing one motif can change every occurrence that reads it.
rows.carry: An editable source tile feeding several chosen construction faces.
rows.test: Change one source cell and predict all repeated occurrences before repainting.

capabilities.title: One source, many surfaces
capabilities.detail: An editable source tile feeding several chosen construction faces.

rows.title: Reflect the reading
rows.learn: Mirroring a lookup differs from reversing stored source rows.
rows.carry: Read an asymmetric motif through normal and reflected surface mappings.
rows.test: Edit through a reflected occurrence; confirm which source address changed.

capabilities.title: Reflect the reading
capabilities.detail: Read an asymmetric motif through normal and reflected surface mappings.

rows.title: A pattern turns the corner
rows.learn: A surface's local frame determines where a pattern is read.
rows.carry: Pattern floors and walls in physical metres while keeping motif data independent.
rows.test: Turn and resize a receiver; check orientation, repeat width and the seam at a corner.

capabilities.title: A pattern turns the corner
capabilities.detail: Pattern floors and walls in physical metres while keeping motif data independent.

rows.title: Compose a symmetry rule
rows.learn: A rule can combine reflection and translation; the motif can hide the difference.
rows.carry: A pattern tool with explicit repeat rules and optional retained woven samples.
rows.test: Compare an asymmetric motif under translation, reflection and glide; do not infer a full classification from one button.

capabilities.title: Compose a symmetry rule
capabilities.detail: A pattern tool with explicit repeat rules and optional retained woven samples.

rows.title: Share a recipe, then diverge
rows.learn: Two surfaces can agree by copying without remaining linked.
rows.carry: Give each room or panel its own pattern recipe, with deliberate copy and link choices.
rows.test: Copy a recipe, edit the second surface, and check whether the first changes as intended.

capabilities.title: Share a recipe, then diverge
capabilities.detail: Give each room or panel its own pattern recipe, with deliberate copy and link choices.

rows.title: A pattern gains a layer
rows.learn: Layers extend addressed values into volume; hiding is not erasing.
rows.carry: Paint or inspect a selected layer of a spatial pattern without deleting other layers.
rows.test: Hide a layer, restore it and compare its original values; use three different indices.

capabilities.title: A pattern gains a layer
capabilities.detail: Paint or inspect a selected layer of a spatial pattern without deleting other layers.

rows.title: The same colour meets another surround
rows.learn: Equal stored colours can appear different in different surroundings.
rows.carry: A comparison tool for panels and decorations whose context changes their appearance.
rows.test: Keep the target values fixed, change the surround, and record what you see without requiring agreement.

capabilities.title: The same colour meets another surround
capabilities.detail: A comparison tool for panels and decorations whose context changes their appearance.

rows.title: A pattern acquires a body
rows.learn: A saved recipe still needs an interpreter and a mapping onto a surface.
rows.carry: Dress a panel, fabric or worn object from the same motif; retain the mapping with the recipe.
rows.test: Compare UV repeat count with metres and reconstruct a saved sample on a second carrier.

capabilities.title: A pattern acquires a body
capabilities.detail: Dress a panel, fabric or worn object from the same motif; retain the mapping with the recipe.

rows.title: Give the connection a direction
rows.learn: A displacement is a relation between positions, not another position.
rows.carry: Direction and distance handles for placing spans, pushes and later moving structures.
rows.test: Move both endpoints equally: the displacement must remain unchanged.

capabilities.title: Give the connection a direction
capabilities.detail: Direction and distance handles for placing spans, pushes and later moving structures.

rows.title: A jump begins with velocity
rows.learn: A prescribed trajectory depends on initial velocity and elapsed time.
rows.carry: A launch-pad proposal with a visible predicted arc and an explicit landing target.
rows.test: Predict the apex and landing; then separately test physical collision and player clearance.

capabilities.title: A jump begins with velocity
capabilities.detail: A launch-pad proposal with a visible predicted arc and an explicit landing target.

rows.title: A push ends; motion continues
rows.learn: Equal forces act differently on different masses.
rows.carry: Pushable construction loads with stated mass and force duration.
rows.test: Apply equal pushes to different masses and watch after the push stops.

capabilities.title: A push ends; motion continues
capabilities.detail: Pushable construction loads with stated mass and force duration.

rows.title: A field acts wherever you are
rows.learn: A position-dependent force can turn a moving body.
rows.carry: Wind and vortex regions threaded through the scaffold, with readable direction markers.
rows.test: Move a probe to two addresses and predict the different accelerations.

capabilities.title: A field acts wherever you are
capabilities.detail: Wind and vortex regions threaded through the scaffold, with readable direction markers.

rows.title: Resistance changes the passage
rows.learn: Drag reads motion; friction and buoyancy are separate choices.
rows.carry: Viscous or frictional zones that change how a body crosses a space.
rows.test: Repeat a drop with resistance off and on, holding gravity and the starting state fixed.

capabilities.title: Resistance changes the passage
capabilities.detail: Viscous or frictional zones that change how a body crosses a space.

rows.title: A spring returns a displaced body
rows.learn: An attachment and a restoring force produce a response.
rows.carry: Spring-mounted cubes and platforms to move around or use, with visible anchors.
rows.test: Pull, release and change damping; distinguish a responding body from a programmed sine.

capabilities.title: A spring returns a displaced body
capabilities.detail: Spring-mounted cubes and platforms to move around or use, with visible anchors.

rows.title: A choreography can drift
rows.learn: Phase offset and rate change have different consequences over time.
rows.carry: Timed obstacle arms or coordinated bridge motion with separate phase and speed controls.
rows.test: Offset one arm once, then change its rate; compare whether the separation stays constant.

capabilities.title: A choreography can drift
capabilities.detail: Timed obstacle arms or coordinated bridge motion with separate phase and speed controls.

rows.title: Attraction has two participants
rows.learn: Mutual attraction changes both bodies rather than fixing one as the centre.
rows.carry: Paired moving masses or orbital obstacles around a protected path.
rows.test: Apply opposite pair forces and compare both motions; keep support collision as a separate test.

capabilities.title: Attraction has two participants
capabilities.detail: Paired moving masses or orbital obstacles around a protected path.

rows.title: A support can be removed
rows.learn: Contact and the support arrangement determine what falls.
rows.carry: Removable legs, props and stepping supports under a loaded construction.
rows.test: Move one support away and observe the first lost contact and subsequent landing.

capabilities.title: A support can be removed
capabilities.detail: Removable legs, props and stepping supports under a loaded construction.

rows.title: One impact starts a sequence
rows.learn: An impulse and later collisions are different events.
rows.carry: A target or obstacle chain driven by one thrown or launched body.
rows.test: Deliver one impulse only; follow which contacts transmit motion afterward.

capabilities.title: One impact starts a sequence
capabilities.detail: A target or obstacle chain driven by one thrown or launched body.

rows.title: Force becomes a way to travel
rows.learn: A held input can keep adding acceleration to the player's movement.
rows.carry: Directional thrust or jump assistance with a legible release state and charge cost to decide.
rows.test: Release the input while retaining the tool; thrust must end without silently erasing velocity.

capabilities.title: Force becomes a way to travel
capabilities.detail: Directional thrust or jump assistance with a legible release state and charge cost to decide.

rows.title: Find a lower value
rows.learn: A local downhill step depends on a stated objective and step size.
rows.carry: A form-search tool that proposes revisions while preserving the original construction.
rows.test: Compare two starts and two steps; report why each run stopped rather than calling every stop optimal.

capabilities.title: Find a lower value
capabilities.detail: A form-search tool that proposes revisions while preserving the original construction.

rows.title: A hanging curve becomes a span
rows.learn: A chosen curve and a physically solved cable are different constructions.
rows.carry: Cable, railing or suspended-bridge profiles with named span and sag inputs.
rows.test: Change sag while keeping anchors fixed; test walking support separately from the drawn curve.

capabilities.title: A hanging curve becomes a span
capabilities.detail: Cable, railing or suspended-bridge profiles with named span and sag inputs.

rows.title: Let distances settle
rows.learn: Rest lengths and fixed anchors constrain a network's relaxation.
rows.carry: A net or cable assembly that can settle between explicit scaffold attachment points.
rows.test: Pin both ends, disturb one node and compare correction counts without moving the anchors.

capabilities.title: Let distances settle
capabilities.detail: A net or cable assembly that can settle between explicit scaffold attachment points.

rows.title: Balance around a pivot
rows.learn: Balance depends on mass and distance under a declared model.
rows.carry: A mobile or counterweighted structure whose supports and omitted masses remain visible.
rows.test: Change one mass and predict the shorter arm; do not equate static equality with dynamic stability.

capabilities.title: Balance around a pivot
capabilities.detail: A mobile or counterweighted structure whose supports and omitted masses remain visible.

rows.title: Sometimes accept the worse step
rows.learn: A search can retain a best result while exploring worse current states.
rows.carry: An optional form-search mode with inspectable temperature, acceptance and best-so-far records.
rows.test: Keep the start fixed, compare cooling schedules and show a worse accepted state separately from the best.

capabilities.title: Sometimes accept the worse step
capabilities.detail: An optional form-search mode with inspectable temperature, acceptance and best-so-far records.

rows.title: Decide what counts as success
rows.learn: A stopped object can still fail a height or stability criterion.
rows.carry: An explicit test for a built form, such as sustained support at a required height.
rows.test: Present a still but too-short candidate and require the test to reject it.

capabilities.title: Decide what counts as success
capabilities.detail: An explicit test for a built form, such as sustained support at a required height.

rows.title: Prescribe a return
rows.learn: Amplitude, frequency and phase govern a periodic position command.
rows.carry: Sine-driven bridges or moving cubes with a retained rest pose.
rows.test: Change phase without changing amplitude; distinguish the command from a body's physical response.

capabilities.title: Prescribe a return
capabilities.detail: Sine-driven bridges or moving cubes with a retained rest pose.

rows.title: Keep the movement's history
rows.learn: A trace records positions and observation times separately.
rows.carry: A movement recorder whose replay can sit beside the moving scaffold.

horizon.title: A 4 × 4 m field returns
horizon.carry: Walk a sine surface. Synchronise bridges through phase and the unit circle.

horizon.title: A route can be sampled
horizon.carry: Perturb nodes, build with a random walk, and negotiate a 4 × 4 m uneven surface. Keep a seed for comparison.

horizon.title: Chance becomes a field
horizon.carry: Correlate neighbouring heights so a rough field can become a continuous terrain.

horizon.title: A surface answers its surroundings
horizon.carry: Let the existing surface respond to position, light or touch; make visual changes legible beside collision.

horizon.title: Neighbours change the structure
horizon.carry: Local states and rules create a changing floor or wall. Give the player a way to inspect one update.

horizon.title: A part contains a return
horizon.carry: Repeat a construction across scales and find the point where its geometry stops being walkable.

horizon.title: A 6 × 6 m growing courtyard
horizon.carry: Let a branching rule grow plants through an inner yard, negotiating the existing frame.

horizon.title: Rules arrange the rooms
horizon.carry: Generate combinations of the accumulated kit, with a traversable route that can be inspected.

horizon.title: The frame can yield
horizon.carry: Add deformation and recovery; preserve a readable relation between contact and material response.

horizon.title: A field acquires a boundary
horizon.carry: Move from sampled values to an inhabitable surface; inspect the threshold that makes it appear.

horizon.title: Combine and subtract bodies
horizon.carry: Make rooms by union, intersection and difference, with collision following the visible result.

horizon.title: Many parts coordinate
horizon.carry: Let moving agents negotiate the structure through local rules; watch collective routes emerge.

horizon.title: Connections become a world
horizon.carry: Expose paths, reachability and disconnection within the structures we have built.

horizon.title: A system changes through examples
horizon.carry: Make the examples and changed behaviour inspectable; compare a learned response with the earlier explicit rules.

horizon.title: The rule meets its limit
horizon.carry: Stage a limit or undecidable demand inside the construction; keep its consequences available to explore.

horizon.title: Compare models of the same world
horizon.carry: Use the accumulated apparatus to compare predictions and observations. The building becomes an experiment.

horizon.title: Build with the unresolved
horizon.carry: Compose a strange walkable world whose limits and alternatives remain visible.

rules: A contribution has a role in the playground as well as an implementation state. A trace, obstacle, decoration or disco need not become structural stock.
A part, assembly, operation and held inventory item are different things.
Before Colour, workshop construction is monochrome; preview highlights are interface cues.
No arbitrary diagonal joints, filled volumes or motors are silently granted to the workshop.
A proposed connection must preserve the same saved construction and its member identities.
Arrays introduces addressed marks and occupancy; Colour later supplies the palette. Painting a surface and adding a cell to a volume are different operations.
Trace as antithesis is a working interpretation: keep its free gesture distinct from the fixed frame, rather than forcing every artifact into building stock.

Whole-spine applications are source-informed proposals. Teaching-plan dependencies and caveats are shown separately; they are not evidence that the carried workshop already implements those operations.
